Usage: hiperf record [options] [command [command-args]]
       Collect performance sampling information of running [command].
       The default options are: -c <all cpu> --cpu-limit 25 -d 10000.0 -e hw-cpu-cycles
       -f 4000 -m 1024 -o /data/local/tmp/perf.data.
   -a
         Collect system-wide information.
         for measures all processes/threads
         This requires CAP_PERFMON (since Linux 5.8) or CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability or a
         /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid value of less than 1.
   --exclude-hiperf
         Don't record events issued by hiperf itself.
   -c <cpuid>[<,cpuid>]...
         cpuid should be 0,1,2...
         Limit the CPU that collects data.
         0 means cpu0, 1 means cpu1 ...
   --cpu-limit <percent>
         Set the max percent of cpu time used for recording.
         percent is in range [1-100], default is 25.
   -d <sec>
         stop in <sec> seconds. floating point number. seconds is in range [0.100-10000.0]
         default is 10000.0
   -f <freq>
         Set event sampling frequency. default is 4000 samples every second.
         check /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_max_sample_rate for maximum allowed frequency
   --period <num>
         Set event sampling period for tracepoint events. recording one sample when <num> events happen.
         The default <num> is 1
   -e <event1[:<u|k>]>[,event1[:<u|k>]]...
         Customize the name of the event that needs to be sampled.
         The name can use the names listed in the list parameter.
         It can also be represented by the value of 0x<hex>.
           u - monitor user space events only
           k - monitor kernel space events only
   -g <event1[:<u|k>]>[,event1[:<u|k>]]...
         Put the events into a group, can set multiple groups by multiple -g
         PMU is required to report data in designated groups
         limited by HW capability, too many events cannot be reported in the same sampling)
   --no-inherit
         Don't trace child processes.
   -p <pid1>[,pid2]...
         Limit the process id of the collection target. Conflicts with the -a option.
   -t <tid1>[,tid2]...
         Limit the thread id of the collection target. Conflicts with the -a option.
   --exclude-tid <tid1>[,tid2]...
         Exclude threads of the collection target by thread ids. Conflicts with the -a option.
   --exclude-thread <tname1>[,tname2]...
         Exclude threads of the collection target by thread names. Conflicts with the -a option.
   --exclude-process <pname1>[,pname2]...
         Exclude processes by process names. Must be used with -a.
   --offcpu
         Trace when threads are scheduled off cpu.
   -j <branch_filter1>[,branch_filter2]...
         taken branch stack sampling, filter can be:
           any: any type of branch
           any_call: any function call or system call
           any_ret: any function return or system call return
           ind_call: any indirect branch
           ind_jmp: any indirect jump
           cond: conditional branches
           call: direct calls, including far (to/from kernel) calls
           u: only when the branch target is at the user level
           k: only when the branch target is in the kernel
         requires at least one of any, any_call, any_ret, ind_call, ind_jmp, cond, call
   -s / --call-stack <fp|dwarf[,size]>
         Setup and enable call stack (stack chain/backtrace) recording, Default is 'fp'.
           the value can be:
             fp: frame pointer
             dwarf: DWARF's CFI - Call Frame Information
               'dwarf,size' set sample stack size, size should be in 8~65528 and 8 byte aligned. 
           as the method to collect the information used to show the call stacks.
   --kernel-callchain
         collect kernel callchain, must used with -s fp/dwarf simultaneously.
   --callchain-useronly
         collect only user callchain.
   --delay-unwind
         If '-s dwarf' used, stack will be unwind while recording, use this option to switch
         to unwind after recording.
   --disable-unwind
         If '-s dwarf' is used, stack will be unwind while recording by default
         use this option to disable unwinding.
   --disable-callstack-expand
         If '-s dwarf' is used, to break the 64k stack limit, callstack is merged by default
         to build more complete call stack. that may not be correct sometimes.
   --enable-debuginfo-symbolic
         If '-s fp/dwarf' is used, symbols in .gnu_debugdata section of an elf, also called minidebuginfo
         will be parsed, if not use this option, we will not parse minidebuginfo by default.
   --clockid <clock_id>
         Set the clock id to use for the various time fields in the perf_event_type records.
         monotonic and monotonic_raw are supported,
         some events might also allow boottime, realtime and clock_tai.
   --pipe_input
         Enable anonymous pipe for the client (calling process) to send control
         commands to the server (hiperf executable program).
         This parameter is designed for system-side C++ interface calls.
         Application developers do not need to pay attention to this parameter
         when using the hiperf command tool.
   --pipe_output
         Enable anonymous pipe for the server (hiperf executable program) to send
         response to the client (calling process).
         This parameter is designed for system-side C++ interface calls.
         Application developers do not need to pay attention to this parameter
         when using the hiperf command tool.
   --symbol-dir <dir>
         Set directory to look for symbol files, used for unwinding. 
   -m <mmap_pages>
         Number of the mmap pages, used to receiving record data from kernel,
         must be a power of two, rang[2,1024], default is 1024.
   --app <package_name>
         Collect profile info for an OHOS app, the app must be debuggable.
         Record will exit if the process is not started within 20 seconds.
   --chkms <millisec>
         Set the interval of querying the <package_name>.
         <millisec> is in range [1-200], default is 10.
   --data-limit <SIZE[K|M|G]>
         Stop recording after SIZE bytes of records. Default is unlimited.
   --append-smo-data
         Output information about the original shared libraries included in SOs
         that support the SMO(Shared library Merge Optimization) feature. 
         The information mainly consists of a mapping table between the PC and
         the original shared library names.
   -o <output_file_name>
         Set output file name, default is /data/local/tmp/perf.data.
   -z
         Compress record data.
   --restart
         Collect performance counter information of application startup.
         Record will exit if the process is not started within 30 seconds.
   --verbose
         Show more detailed reports.
   --control <command>
         Control sampling by <command>, the <command> can be:
           prepare: set arguments and prepare sampling
           start: start sampling
           pause: pause sampling
           resume: resume sampling
           output: output sampling data
           stop: stop sampling
   --dedup_stack
         Remove duplicated stacks in perf record, conflicts with -a, only restrain using with -p
   --cmdline-size <size>
         set value to /sys/kernel/tracing/saved_cmdlines_size
         the value should be between 512 and 4096
   --report
         Report with callstack after record. Conflicts with the -a option.
   --backtrack
         Collect data of the previous period. only restrain using with --control.
   --backtrack-sec
         If '--backtrack' is used, stop in <sec> seconds. seconds is in range [5-30]
         default is 10
   --dumpoptions
         Dump command options.
